about: The Port District anchors the city's holiday photo displays. The city lists three photo stops here: four moonlight arches that lead to a 12-foot illuminated flower walk-through ornament, a poinsettia flower arch, and the Port sign lit with a glowing anchor.

The city publishes a day by day schedule at The Port District. Santa and local artisans are at the Botanical Gardens November 27 to 29, the Grinch is there December 4 to 6, and festive characters, vendors and food trucks return December 11 to 13. Voices of Valencia plays live music at the Botanical Gardens Pavilion on December 19 from 6 to 8 PM. The schedule is subject to change.

To cut traffic, the city runs a Park and Win contest. Visitors who park at Tom Hooper Park, Veterans Park at Rivergate or the U.S. Post Office on SE Veterans Memorial Parkway can walk the boardwalk to the lights and enter a drawing. The city also offers a downloadable PDF flyer for the season.

PSLinLights as a whole is the city's holiday season of more than two million twinkling lights, running from November 27 through December 31. The city lists two walk-through light experiences, a citywide residential lights contest, an interactive map, fourteen photo displays and a scavenger hunt in search of glowing sandhill cranes. WPBF 25 sponsors the season.
The Port District trails are the larger of the two walk-through experiences, which makes them the best choice for a long evening stroll with children who like to see animals made of light.

The Pioneer Express train is the one paid extra at the Port District, at $5 for kids and parents. Everything else on the trails, including the displays and the Botanical Gardens programs, is listed as free by the city. The Port District sits on SE Westmoreland Blvd, and the trails link the Event Lawn with the Botanical Gardens.
faq: What is the nightly schedule?
Dusk to 9 PM nightly from November 27 to December 31, 2026, and the city's date list shows 5:30 to 9 PM.
How much is the train ride?
The city lists the Pioneer Express train at $5 for kids and parents.
Is there a quieter night for sensory needs?
Yes. On Thursday and Friday, December 3 and 4, the lights come on earlier, from 5 PM to dusk, for people with sensory disabilities.
Where can I park?
The city points visitors to Tom Hooper Park, Veterans Park at Rivergate and the U.S. Post Office for its Park and Win contest.
How many light experiences does the city run?
Two walk-through experiences, one at The Port District and one at the community center, plus a map of decorated homes.

about: The community center is one of five spots where the city invites families to take holiday photos. Here the display is a 12-foot walk-through ornament in vibrant red and shimmering silver.

The city lists other photo displays around Port St. Lucie. City Hall Building A at 121 SW Port St. Lucie Blvd has a 14-foot walk-through wreath arch and a 12-foot snowman arch. McChesney Park, 1585 SW Cashmere Blvd, has a 10-foot Happy Holidays card with a snowman family. Midport Lake Neighborhood Park has a 12-foot gingerbread house with a gingerbread family and candy canes.

Families who want to keep going can use the city's Holiday Lights Map for a self guided drive past contest homes. The city asks drivers to remember the 25 mph residential speed limit and not to block driveways. A scavenger hunt for glowing sandhill cranes is also part of the season.

The community center plaza is a smaller walk-through than the Port District trails, so it works well as a short outing before bedtime. The city lists the same free admission and the same nightly schedule through December 31.

Residents decorate their own homes for the city's PSLinLights Home Decorating Contest, and the Holiday Lights Map shows where to find them. Veterans Memorial Park at 2100 SE Veterans Memorial Parkway has four patriotic light displays: a tank, a paratrooper, an American flag and a Humvee.

For a different feel from the Port District trails, the plaza at the community center is a compact space where families can see thousands of lights in one spot. It is the same building where Pancakes with Santa breakfast is held on December 19.
faq: Is the community center display free?
Yes. The city lists free admission from November 27 to December 31.
What is sensory friendly time?
From 5 PM to 6 PM the music is turned off for people with sensory disabilities.
What is the address?
Port St. Lucie Community Center, 2195 SE Airoso Blvd, Port St. Lucie, FL 34984.
Is there a driving map of home displays?
Yes. The city publishes a Holiday Lights Map of contest homes and festive destinations.
Where are the other photo displays?
City Hall, the MIDFLORIDA Event Center, McChesney Park, Veterans Memorial Park and Midport Lake Neighborhood Park, according to the city.

about: The Botanical Gardens host a rotating set of weekend programs during PSLinLights. Santa and local artisans are there November 27 to 29, the Grinch is there December 4 to 6, and festive characters, vendors, crafts and food trucks return December 11 to 13.
The Botanical Gardens event sits next to the Port District light trails, which are open nightly until 9 PM. Visitors can walk from the gardens along the lit path toward the Event Lawn.
On Saturday, December 19, the Botanical Gardens Pavilion hosts Voices of Valencia, a live music evening from 6 to 8 PM, which is a separate event from the Grinch weekend.

Hosting weekends rotate at the Botanical Gardens. The first weekend is Santa with local artisans, the second is the Grinch with artisans and food trucks, and the third is festive characters, vendors, crafts and food trucks. Each of these runs from 5:30 PM to 9 PM.

The city's PSLinLights news story lists the Grinch weekend in its Port District section, and the city flyer for the season is available as a PDF. Families who want a quiet visit can use the sensory friendly nights on December 3 and 4, which come just before the Grinch weekend.

The hamlethub listing for this event, which cites the city's schedule, also describes the Grinch weekend as an evening with local artisans, crafts and food trucks, and notes that admission is free with donations accepted.

For parents, the city's schedule is the quickest way to plan. Santa and local artisans take the first weekend, the Grinch takes the second, and festive characters return the third. The Botanical Gardens are open for these programs from 5:30 PM to 9 PM, and the nightly lights run until 9 PM.
faq: Which nights does the Grinch appear?
December 4, 5 and 6, 2026.
What time is it?
5:30 PM to 9 PM each night, according to the city's schedule.
Is it free?
Yes. Admission is free and donations are accepted.
Where are the Botanical Gardens?
2410 SE Westmoreland Blvd, Port St. Lucie, FL 34952.
What else is at the Botanical Gardens that weekend?
Local artisans, crafts and food trucks, according to the city.
Is the Grinch there every night of PSLinLights?
No. The city says the Grinch appears December 4 to 6 only.
Is there a cost to enter the gardens event?
Admission is free and donations are accepted.

about: The city's EngagePSL program brings its departments to the Botanical Gardens for a night of community fun. Families can visit City booths and local business vendors, enjoy music and crafts, and take photos with Santa. Questions go to the city Communications office at 772-871-5219 or pslcommunications@cityofpsl.com.
The Youth Council runs the movie night. The city says donations are accepted for the movie and popcorn, while the rest of the evening is free.

The night before, River Nights returns to the Event Lawn at The Port District on Thursday, December 10, from 5:30 to 8:30 PM. River Nights is a free monthly event on the second Thursday from October through April, with live music and food trucks.

The program is subject to change, according to the city, so check the city page before you go. The Botanical Gardens are at 2410 SE Westmoreland Blvd, about a short walk from the Event Lawn light trails.
The city tags this event for kids, families, community members and seniors, so it is aimed at a wide mix of ages. Bring a lawn chair or blanket for the movie if you want to sit comfortably.

Because the Youth Council hosts the film, the movie is a family friendly screening held right at the gardens, and there is no ticketing: the city lists the cost as free with donations accepted for the movie and popcorn.

Visitors can stop by City booths to learn about local government programs and meet staff in a relaxed setting. The city lists the night for families, community members and seniors. It begins at 5 PM, and the Youth Council film starts at 6:30 PM.
faq: What movie is shown?
Home Alone, at 6:30 PM, hosted by the Youth Council.
Does it cost anything?
The city lists the event as free, with donations accepted for the movie and popcorn.
Where is it?
Port St. Lucie Botanical Gardens, 2410 SE Westmoreland Blvd.
What else is on that weekend?
Festive characters, local vendors, crafts and food trucks are at the Botanical Gardens December 11 to 13.
Who can I contact?
The city Communications office at 772-871-5219 or pslcommunications@cityofpsl.com.
When does the movie start?
6:30 PM, after the music, crafts and Santa photos.
Is it good for young kids?
The city tags it for kids and families, and it includes crafts and Santa photos.

about: The city names five food and dessert vendors for the night: El Hay Bendito, Rineboi Churassco Grill, Rosita's Aguas Y Delicias, Si Mi Reyna Antojitos and Tacos Downtown. The band, Jamboree Latin Band, is led by Carlos Cabrera and plays salsa, merengue, cumbia and bachata.
Noche Buena sits in the same Port District complex as the nightly PSLinLights trails. The anchor display includes a 12-foot walk-through flower ornament and the glowing Port sign.

Questions go to the city's Special Events Department at 772-344-4139 or specialevents@cityofpsl.com. The same evening, the museum's Christmas open house runs from 5:30 to 8:30 PM and a free Grinch movie night starts at 6 PM at the Police Athletic League Gym.
Noche Buena is listed as a community event for kids and families, and the city describes it as a night of cultural warmth and joyful entertainment that brings family and friends together.
The vendors serve dishes and treats inspired by traditional Noche Buena celebrations, so it is a good way for kids to try new foods in a lively setting.
The event is one of the Port District's headline December nights. It starts at 5 PM, the live music begins at 5:30 PM, and the whole event wraps up at 9 PM.

The program is subject to change, according to the city. Admission is free, and the Special Events Department lists no sign up or tickets for the evening, so families can simply walk in from the Port District grounds on SE Westmoreland Blvd.
faq: Who plays at Noche Buena?
The Jamboree Latin Band, a six piece Miami based group, starting at 5:30 PM.
Which food vendors are listed?
El Hay Bendito, Rineboi Churassco Grill, Rosita's Aguas Y Delicias, Si Mi Reyna Antojitos and Tacos Downtown.
Who sponsors it?
Florida Blue.
Who can I contact?
The city's Special Events Department at 772-344-4139 or specialevents@cityofpsl.com.
Is it a kids event?
The city tags it for kids and families as well as the whole community.
